metadata.scope: Rigid clamp couplers, flexible/helical couplers, Oldham couplers, jaw couplers.

material_suggestions.use_case: rigid and flexible machined shaft couplers
material_suggestions.notes: Good strength; clamp slit gives enough flex for clamping force.
Orient vertical for best torsional strength in layers.
Self-lubricating; good sliding contact with hubs.

standards_used.name: General coupler sizing
standards_used.note: OD ≥ max(shaft_a, shaft_b) + 8 mm wall each side; length 25–40 mm for NEMA17 to T8.

standards_used.name: DIN 6885A keyway
standards_used.applies_to: D-flat and keyway on shaft ends
standards_used.note: Flat depth typically 1 mm for ø5–6 mm shafts.

output_policy.openscad_code: Geometry-only OpenSCAD with named parameters, one module, and no prose.

parts.name: Fixed helical beam shaft coupling with through screw holes
main_features: outer cylinder body with chamfered ends
bore A from bottom end (shaft_a diameter) to centre
bore B from top end (shaft_b diameter) to centre
helical beam relief grooves on OD for torsional compliance
two radial through-screw holes for shaft retention
design_rules: Helical cuts use linear_extrude(height=length+2, twist=-(360*turns), slices=300, center=true). NEVER use rotate_extrude for helical cuts — it creates a torus at fixed radius, not a helix.
The outer body cylinder is the POSITIVE volume. Bore and helical slots are SUBTRACTED from it. NEVER add the bore cylinder in union() and subtract the same bore again — they cancel out.
Helical slot 2D profile: translate([slot_r, 0]) square([wall_depth+2, slot_w], center=true) where slot_r = bore_d/2 + wall_depth/2.
For a 2-start coupler: two slots offset by 180°: for(i=[0:1]) rotate([0,0,i*180]) linear_extrude(...).
bore_a is drilled from the bottom end; bore_b from the top end; both coaxial on Z axis.
Wall between each bore and OD must be >= 3 mm: (outer_d - bore_d) / 2 >= 3.
Set screw holes are radial: translate([0, outer_d/2, end_z]) rotate([90,0,0]) cylinder(...).
Do NOT declare string metadata variables like manufacturing = "fdm" in the OpenSCAD output.
validation_criteria: bore_a cylinder from bottom end in difference
bore_b cylinder from top end in difference (different diameter)
bores do not overlap beyond centre — each shaft clamps independently
radial screw holes cut through body for shaft retention
failure_modes: rotate_extrude used for helical cuts — produces a torus at fixed radius, not a helix; coupling body will look like a donut, not a coupler
bore cylinder added in union() then subtracted in difference() — they cancel out, leaving no bore and no outer body
circular_grooves() (horizontal rings) used instead of helical cuts — creates a disc coupler, not a helical beam coupler
helix_point function defined but never used — dead code that contributes no geometry
manufacturing string variable in output — violates output policy
single uniform bore — both shafts same diameter, wrong for different-size shafts
bores side-by-side instead of coaxial — misaligned shafts

constraint_checks.expression: bore_a and bore_b both centered on Z axis
constraint_checks.message: Both shaft bores must be coaxial on the same central axis.
Wall between bore_b and OD must be at least 3 mm to retain structural integrity.
Helical beam coupling must have two different bore sizes for the two shaft diameters.

required_features: Solid chamfered coupling body from rotate_extrude profile
Bore A from bottom end (shaft_a + 0.2mm) to just past centre
Bore B from top end (shaft_b + 0.2mm) to just past centre
Repeated circular beam relief grooves on OD
Two radial through screw holes with counterbores on both sides

parts.name: Rigid split-clamp shaft coupler
required_features: Cylindrical body with two stepped bores
Clamping screw holes crossing the slit
design_rules: Put the outer cylinder as the only positive body volume in difference(); bores, slit, screw holes, and chamfer are all subtractive cutters.
Bore A enters from the bottom: translate([0,0,-length/2-0.5]) cylinder(h=length/2+1, d=bore_a, center=false).
Bore B enters from the centre/top side: translate([0,0,-0.5]) cylinder(h=length/2+1, d=bore_b, center=false).
Radial slit cutter: translate([0, outer_d/4, 0]) cube([split_gap, outer_d/2+2, length+2], center=true). It is thin in X, reaches from the outside to the bore, and must be subtracted.
Clamping screw holes run along Y with rotate([90,0,0]) and are offset to x=outer_d/4 so they cross the slit through solid wall material instead of drilling down the bore axis.
Use two clamping screws, one in each shaft section, typically at z=-length/2+offset and z=length/2-offset.
Chamfer cutters must be subtracted from the edge; never translate a cone below the body and add it as positive geometry.
Do NOT declare string metadata variables (manufacturing, material, etc.) in OpenSCAD code.
failure_modes: slit cube placed in implicit union inside body() - slit is added as solid material instead of removed
rotate([0,90,0]) on slit cube - turns the slit cutter into the wrong orientation
bore cylinders use center=true with non-zero translate - bore extents become easy to misplace
clamp holes along Z with no rotate - holes are parallel to the shaft, not crossing the slit
clamp holes at x=0 on the bore axis - holes pass through the bore void instead of clamp wall material
single clamp screw at z=0 - only one screw for the whole coupler; use one per bore section
chamfer translated below the body and added in union - adds cone outside body instead of chamfering the edge
